*** Note: This is the old review I left after the game crashed multiple times on me. Just 1 hour after posting this I received very helpful support that fixed all issues easily. Therefore please look bellow for my actual review. I'll leave the original here ***
Original: I would love to recommend this game as it is probably the most realistic hacking sim out there, but I can't get past a game breaking bug very early into the game. Nothing seems to fix this issue: Relaunching the game, starting a new campaign, deleting the old campaign or following the instructions exactly one step at a time. Hitting reply on the third email you receive will reliably crash the game completly and thus you can not possibly progress. Edit/Actual:
Hacknet is a realistic - if not even the most realistic - hacking simulation game.
Pro:
- realistic (comes very close to actual linux/unix terminal commands and network architecture for example)
- many interesting mechanics
- easy to pick up
- includes eastereggs
- fun to play
- very reasonably priced (if not underpriced)
- you can save at any point
Con:
- Some might find parts of this game repetitive, though this is not much of a concern to me
- as stated above, the game used to crash. But thanks to the quick support I received all problems were fixed as of now.

I would definitly recommend this game if you enjoy puzzle-ish games and/or hacking sims. You have to know nothing about hacking to quickly get into this game but it is fun even if you are a programmer or hacker yourself.

reviews.review:
Hacknet is a detective/puzzle game that nails the [i]aesthetics[/i] of computer hacking so well that it feels like a somewhat authentic computer hacking experience. 

It strips away all the elements of real computer hacking that would bog the experience down - there's no long periods of waiting on hashcat, no sifting through packet captures which don't actually have anything interesting, no calling a support desk and hoping they reset a password for you. What it leaves behind is all of the most interesting bits: actually breaking into some system, mapping out a network, hopping from computer to computer until you find what you're looking for. The game delivers on that experience in a way other games (such as Uplink) don't for me.

This game has done an incredible job capturing the spirit of hacking. Although by necessity, the procedures are highly simplified, the approach is rooted in practice and demonstrates how even secure networks can be compromised through a domino effect of lesser vulnerabilities. Topple the weakest link and the strongest will follow. Your target may be impenetrable at first. But what about cracking the defenses on an unsecured edge workstation -- breaking into an employee's laptop is far simpler. Once in, you can read the owner's emails, learn their passwords, snoop through files of mostly useless documents for the juicy bits, and finally, advantages and privileges under arm, launch additional attacks deep into the heart of the network. It's neat, and you won't have Interpol knocking at your door afterwards.

PREFACE: I only played this game for one hour, and this may be a biased review, but so far I didn't see anything worth pursuing. The game may get interesting further down, but it just didn't pique my interesting so far.

This game does way too much hand holding to be enjoyable. If you're a casual gamer who wants to get the feeling that you're a cool hacker, go for it, but if you want any actual challenge, this game is not for you.

The whole game is just reading long emails trying to get the important information, then running the same sequence of commands over and over for every challenge. Every time they want to make it harder, they just add one more command to this sequence and repeat the same process.

There was very little problem solving or experimenting happening, which to me is what hacking is all about. Trying things out yourself and learning new tools. Not someone telling you what to do each step of the way.

The terminal interface was neat and the soundtrack was banging, but the game was just too bland and repetitive to be enjoyable.

To be frank, I've taken this game and played it for at least three times the amount of time steam has recorded me on it. And in all honesty, this game has tons of charm. Yes, the storyline is short, however the immensely fitting soundtrack and numerous textual gems in the game assists in making this game amazing. There will be points in this game where you will laugh at a silly request or character, or even a small piece of dialogue, and there will be points in which you will need to set the game down for an hour or so to contemplate the actions you've decided to take, or the gravity of the mistake you've potentially made. The atmosphere generated by the soundtrack is immensely fitting for the gameplay, and (in my personal opinion) does make you feel rather devious as you weave through the security measures on a character's computer to further the game. And when your "computer" crashes for the first time, expect to freak out for a second. It is just a game, but some of the featues that make the game such an excellent hacking sim can, and will, startle you. :P

With the upcoming additions and DLC, including multiplayer and new storylines, I wouldn't hesitate to pick this game up again and start playing.

Best hacking "sim" game i've ever  played since uplink..

Hacknet is a story-focused visual novel where hacking is used as the framing device for discovering a world in a way I don't think I really saw until it was released. Exploring networks of private computers and peering into people's personal files to uncover embarassing secrets, deep corporate conspiracies and more is quite satisfying to do in this game -- but again, if you are expecting legitimately deep game mechanics, you might be disappointed in the game.

The extension framework deserves a special mention, as it allows community members to use Hacknet as a means to tell their own elaborate stories, using all of the same tools that the base experience does. This allows for a theoretically infinite amount of content, if you want to get more of your fill of hacking-themed stories.
One of the best hacking games i've ever played, alongside Uplink, and in some ways this even blows Uplink out of the water. Well worth its price and crazy value for money when on sale.
